subject: Question about one-time capacity line item on Oct invoice
messages:
From: Amelia Carson <amelia@lumenize.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@lumenize.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected one-time charge on Oct invoice

Hi Vivek,

We were reviewing our October invoice and there is a one-time line item for $18,432 labeled 'one-time capacity top-up (Sep)'. We had a short-term campaign in late September and did increase concurrency, but we understood that our Dedicated pool had a buffer and that overages would be capped per our renewal conversation in July.

Can you help explain what this charge is for? I attached the invoice PDF. If this is a retroactive true-up, we need the usage detail and how it maps to our committed capacity.

Thanks —
Amelia
Billing & Ops
Lumenize Inc.

Attachment: Lumenize_Invoice_202610.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Carson <amelia@lumenize.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-time charge on Oct invoice

Hi Amelia —

Thanks for flagging this and sending the invoice. I'm looping in Ben (Finance) and Laura (your AM) to pull a usage report and reconcile the charge. Initial next steps:

- Ben: can you pull the detailed token/slot usage for Lumenize for Sep 1–30 and the invoice calculus that produced the $18,432 one-time line?
- Laura: can you confirm whether Lumenize had any temporary capacity increases or scheduled bursts that were outside the committed pool?

We'll aim to get a reconciliation back to you within 48 hours. Apologies for the customer experience — we'll make this as painless as possible.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: usage export + initial reconciliation (Lumenize)

Vivek / Laura — attaching the usage export and my quick reconciliation. Notes:

- Attached CSV (redwood-usage-export-202609.csv) shows two days (2026-09-22 and 2026-09-23) where concurrent slot consumption spiked to ~3.1x the committed baseline. Those spikes triggered billing under the overage policy.
- The invoice calculation includes both the overage token charge and an automated "one-time capacity top-up" that our billing engine applies when burst capacity exceeds X% of committed for >48 hours. The combined math yields $18,432.
- However, on manual review there appears to be a duplication: the automated top-up and the per-token overage were applied for the same windows — that double-counts about $5,000.

Recommendation: propose an immediate one-time credit of $5,000 to offset the duplication, and offer to apply the remaining $13,432 as either a credit or a reissued invoice with a note for internal accounting. Additionally, suggest a formal amendment to increase committed capacity from 12 concurrent slots to 18 for the remaining 8 months of the term, prorated, to cover the usage pattern and avoid future bursts.

Attachment: redwood-usage-export-202609.csv

—Ben
Director, Revenue Operations

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Carson <amelia@lumenize.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-time charge on Oct invoice — proposed resolution

Hi Amelia,

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Quick summary of findings from our reconciliation team (Ben):

- There were two high-concurrency days in late September that triggered burst billing.
- Our billing engine applied both per-token overage charges and an automated one-time capacity top-up for the same usage window; that resulted in duplicate billing of approximately $5,000.

Proposed remediation options (pick one):
1) Apply a one-time credit of $5,000 immediately to your October invoice and reissue a corrected invoice for the remaining $13,432; OR
2) Apply the $5,000 credit and also apply the $13,432 as a credit balance to your account (recommended if you'd like to avoid another invoicing step).

Separately, to avoid recurrence we can execute a short-term amendment: increase your committed concurrency from 12 -> 18 for the remaining 8 months at a prorated rate. With that amendment in place the projected monthly overage exposure is negligible based on Sept patterns. I attached a draft amendment we can route through DocuSign if you'd like to proceed.

Which option do you prefer for handling the $13,432? If you want the amendment we can route it today and, once signed, we'll apply the agreed credit path and reissue the invoice if necessary.

Thanks —
Vivek
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-amendment-lumenize-202611.docx
Related link: https://docusign.com/link/proposed-amendment-7890

From: Amelia Carson <amelia@lumenize.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@lumenize.com
Date: 2026-11-01T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-time charge on Oct invoice — proposed resolution

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the clear write-up and for catching the duplication. We'd like to take option 2: apply the $5,000 correction as a credit and leave the $13,432 as a credit balance on our account so our finance team doesn't need a reissued invoice for reconciliation this quarter.

We also want to proceed with the amendment to increase to 18 concurrent slots for the remaining 8 months — please route the DocuSign and cc our procurement lead (procurement@lumenize.com). Once the amendment is signed, please confirm the credits applied and the updated monthly committed rate.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Amelia
Billing & Ops
Lumenize Inc.
